findings.title: Cleanup ticker unintentionally changed from 10m to 1m
findings.body: File pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go line 77 changes the background cleanup ticker from every 10 minutes to every 1 minute. That ticker drives all cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, short URLs, query history, annotations), not just annotations, so this increases DB and IO load 10x. The PR description only mentions annotation deadlocks and does not justify this. It looks like debug leftover and should be reverted.

findings.title: Leftover debug logging at Error level dumps tens of thousands of IDs
findings.body: File pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go lines 534,537,554,557,576,579 log every cleanup batch with r.log.Error including the full ids slice, cond and nil err. With the configured batch size up to 32767 this dumps tens of thousands of IDs at Error level on every cleanup cycle, spamming error logs, triggering false alerts, filling disks and hurting performance. These should be Debug or removed before merge.

findings.title: Batch loop terminates on affected==0 instead of fetched==0 causing under-delete
findings.body: File pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go function untilDoneOrCancelled stops when affected == 0. The new cleanup splits work into fetchIDs then deleteByIDs, so affected is rows actually deleted, not rows found. If IDs disappear between SELECT and DELETE due to concurrent delete, affected can be 0 while fetch returned non-empty and many rows remain, causing premature exit and leaving expired rows until the next cycle. Termination should be based on len(ids)==0 / fetched count, not RowsAffected.

findings.title: SQLite parameter-limit bypass checks configured batch size not actual arg count
findings.body: File pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go line 608 decides to inline IDs into SQL when r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999 instead of when len(ids) > 999. The limit that matters is the number of placeholders actually sent. This mis-check inlines unnecessarily when the batch is small, and more importantly the else-branch can still exceed variable limits on other DBs or when batch size is raised, and builds the IN list with repeated fmt.Sprintf in a loop which is O(n^2) for large batches like 32767.
